title: Injective and surjective maps of presheaves are the monomorphisms and epimorphisms

difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the injective and surjective maps of presheaves of sets, as defined componentwise, with the monomorphisms and epimorphisms of the category of presheaves, and characterizes isomorphisms as the maps that are both (statement lines 372-378). The proof is a complete argument in three parts: injectivity is compared with monicity through the Yoneda identification of elements with natural transformations from representables (proof lines 381-403); surjectivity is compared with the epimorphism property by constructing the presheaf of pushouts along the components and using the two canonical maps into it (proof lines 406-442); and the characterization of isomorphisms is obtained by combining pointwise inverses into a natural transformation (proof lines 445-453). The non-formal content is the pushout construction in the second part and the Yoneda translation in the first. The claim is H2: three written-out equivalences with each input named.
